Day 4: Costa Maya excursions
Day 4 · Wednesday

Costa Maya

Costa Maya, Mexico
Mayan ruins · Mahahual · Mesoamerican Barrier Reef · Bacalar Lagoon
Costa Maya is the quieter, less-developed cousin of the bigger Mexican cruise ports — that's a feature, not a bug. The port itself is a controlled cruise village; the real action is either inland at the Mayan ruins or down the coast at Mahahual's laid-back beach clubs. Below are the four excursion paths most travelers take. Most can be booked through the ship or independently — independent operators typically run 30-40% less than the ship excursions.
Cultural · Half-Day
Chacchoben Mayan Ruins
The most popular and accessible Mayan site from Costa Maya — about 55-60 min by bus inland. Large temples and platforms dating to ~700 AD, with a guided tour of the ceremonial center known as "The Place of Red Corn." Great pick if you want one anchoring cultural experience for the day.
~4 hoursAir-conditioned busGuidedAll ages
Adventure · Full-Day
Bacalar "Lake of Seven Colors"
A longer drive (~2 hrs each way) but worth it for the experience. Bacalar's freshwater lagoon is famous for its iridescent turquoise hues — boat tour, swimming, and lunch typically included. This is the bucket-list excursion of Costa Maya for travelers who want something genuinely different.
~7-8 hoursBus + boatLunch incl.Long day
Beach · Flexible
Mahahual Beach Club Day Pass
Twenty-minute transfer to Mahahual's seaside beach clubs (Maya Chan, Nacional Beach Club, Tropicante are the standouts). Beach chairs, umbrellas, food and drinks included on most all-inclusive passes. Perfect if you just want a relaxed day on the Mesoamerican Reef coastline. The reef is right offshore — bring or rent a snorkel.
4-6 hours flexibleAll-inclusive optionsEasy pace
Water · Active
Reef Snorkel + Beach
Small-group boat snorkel on the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef — sea turtles, stingrays, tropical fish in their natural habitat. Most tours pair the reef portion with a beach club afterwards for lunch and a swim. Solid combo if you want both water adventure and a beach day in the same outing.
~5 hoursSnorkel gear incl.Must swimUnderwater photos

Agent recommendation for Costa Maya If you've never seen a Mayan site, do Chacchoben — it's the highest-impact use of the day and you're back to the ship with time for the port village. If you've done ruins before and want something special, Bacalar is unique to this port and you won't find it elsewhere on the itinerary. If you're cruise-tired by Wednesday, the Mahahual beach club pass is the no-stress option.
Day 5: Roatán
Day 5 · Thursday

Roatán, Honduras

Roatán, Honduras
West Bay Beach · Mesoamerican Reef snorkeling · sloths & monkeys · island tours
Roatán is the under-the-radar gem of the western Caribbean. The pace is slow, the beaches are world-class, and the Mesoamerican Reef runs right along the coast — meaning you can literally walk off the beach into 80 ft of visibility snorkel water. Most travelers report Roatán as the surprise highlight of the whole trip.
Beach · Easy
West Bay Beach Day
Roatán's #1-rated beach: powdered white sand, turquoise water, and the reef accessible right from shore. Most popular pass is at Bananarama Dive & Beach Resort — Caribbean ambiance, mahogany structures, palms, drinks at the swim-up. About 20 min from the cruise pier.
4-6 hours flexibleDay passSnorkel right offshore
Water · Iconic
Reef Snorkel — Tabyana / West Bay
Guided small-group snorkel on Roatán's section of the Mesoamerican Reef. Two stops: a shallow drop-off (tangs, snapper, angel fish) and the wall ("the abyss") with 80-120 ft visibility. Bring an underwater camera — sea turtles and rays are common sightings.
3-4 hoursGear providedMust be swimmer~$55 indep.
Wildlife · Family
Daniel Johnson's Monkey & Sloth Hangout
Hold an actual sloth. Hold an actual monkey. Scarlet macaws on your shoulder. This isn't a zoo — it's a sanctuary where you can interact directly with rescued and rehabilitated animals. One of the most photo-worthy stops on any Caribbean cruise. Pairs naturally with a half-day West Bay beach add-on.
~2 hours at sanctuaryCash paymentAll ages
Adventure · Combo
Zip-n-Dip — Canopy + Beach
Soar through the rainforest canopy on one of Roatán's zipline courses (15 platforms, 1,000-ft fast cable on the popular South Shore route), then transfer to West Bay Beach for the rest of the afternoon. The "best valued" combo on the island per local operators. Adrenaline plus relaxation.
~5-6 hoursActiveBeach includedAge 8+
Cultural · Easygoing
Roatán Island Tour
Air-conditioned minivan circuit of the island — Coxen Hole, Oak Ridge fishing villages, Jonesville mangrove tunnels, scenic overlooks, with a beach stop included. Good for first-timers who want to see the whole island and don't necessarily want to commit to one beach for the whole day.
~4-5 hoursA/C transportLight pace
All-Inclusive · Splurge
Little French Key
A private island resort surrounded by turquoise water — mangroves, gardens, white sand walkways, and an exotic animal rescue (jaguars, tigers, black swans). Day pass typically includes food, drinks, water sports rentals, and beach access. The premium-experience pick if you want one upgraded day.
Full dayAll-inclusiveAnimal rescue on-site

Agent recommendation for Roatán Most travelers' best day on this whole cruise is Roatán. If you do nothing else: West Bay Beach day pass is the single highest-rated experience, and the reef snorkel right off the beach means you can do snorkeling without booking a separate tour. The sloth and monkey hangout is the photo memory — pair it with a half-day at West Bay if you can. Skip the canopy if heights aren't your thing.
Day 6: Cozumel
Day 6 · Friday

Cozumel, Mexico

Cozumel, Mexico
Palancar & Columbia reefs · El Cielo starfish sandbar · San Gervasio · beach clubs
Cozumel is the island Jacques Cousteau put on the diving map — visibility reaches 200+ feet on the right day. It's the busiest of your three ports (multiple ships in on most days), but with the right excursion you skip the cruise-port crowds entirely. The reefs here are some of the best in the entire Caribbean, period.
Water · Bucket List
Palancar + Columbia Reef + El Cielo
The signature Cozumel snorkel: drift-snorkel over Palancar's coral canyons (where eagle rays glide), float across Columbia Reef (sea turtle territory), then anchor at El Cielo — a heaven-clear sandbar named for its pure-white bottom and resident starfish. Three reefs, one boat, one day. The single best snorkel experience on the entire itinerary.
~4 hoursSmall groupDrinks/snacksMust swim
Beach Park · Family
Chankanaab Adventure Beach Park
Cozumel's most popular beach park — snorkel right off the beach (no boat needed), botanical gardens, a Mayan archaeological replica, dolphin and sea lion programs (extra), restaurants and bars. Day pass options run all-inclusive. The all-in-one pick for travelers who want options without committing to one activity.
Full day flexibleDay passSnorkel from shore
Cultural · Quiet
San Gervasio Mayan Ruins
Cozumel's most significant Mayan site — a quieter, more intimate alternative to mainland ruins. Once a ceremonial center dedicated to the fertility goddess Ixchel, where Mayan women historically traveled by canoe to make pilgrimage. About 7 miles from San Miguel. Pairs well with a half-day beach add-on afterwards.
~3 hours at siteGuided toursLight walking
Beach Club · Premium
Mr. Sancho's or Nachi-Cocom
Two of Cozumel's top all-inclusive beach clubs. Mr. Sancho's is the bigger, more-amenity one (pools, water sports, multiple bars, full dining); Nachi-Cocom is the quieter, capacity-limited alternative (250-person cap means it never feels crowded). All-inclusive food and drinks all day, beach chairs, hot tubs, restaurants, optional massages.
Full day flexible~$55-100 ppAll food & drinks
Adventure · Active
ATV / Jeep / RZR Jungle Tour
Off-road through Cozumel's jungle interior — backroads, El Cedral village (the island's oldest Mayan settlement), and a beach stop. Most operators bundle the off-road portion with a beach club access pass and lunch. Active alternative for travelers who've snorkeled enough on the trip already.
~5-6 hoursActiveBeach add-onAge 18+ to drive
Glass-Bottom · Easy
Glass-Bottom Boat Reef Tour
For anyone who wants to see the reef without getting in the water — guided tour over the same Palancar/Columbia reef formations from the comfort of a glass-bottom boat. Most tours include a brief snorkel option for those who want it. Lower-effort way to see the marine life.
~2-3 hoursNo swimming requiredAll ages
Pick one excursion for Cozumel. The three-reef snorkel is the marquee experience here.

Agent recommendation for Cozumel The Palancar/Columbia/El Cielo three-reef snorkel is genuinely the most spectacular water experience on this whole cruise — if there's one excursion to splurge on, it's this one. If reef-snorkeling isn't your thing or you've done it earlier in the week, Mr. Sancho's beach club is the easy all-inclusive day. Skip San Gervasio if you've already done Chacchoben at Costa Maya — they'll feel similar and you'll get more out of a beach day instead.
